question: What happens if air is NOT removed from a hydraulic brake system?

options.text: The brakes feel spongy and less effective.

solution:
The correct answer is __The brakes feel spongy and less effective**(Option 4)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Air in the hydraulic brake system__ leads to spongy and less effective brakes.
 
• Air is compressible, unlike the brake fluid, which reduces the efficiency of the hydraulic system.
 
• When air is present, the brake pedal needs to be pressed harder and further to achieve the same braking force.
 
• It can result in delayed braking response, which is dangerous in emergency situations.
 
• Removing air through a process called "brake bleeding" ensures optimal performance of the braking system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Hydraulic Brake System:**

 
 
• It works on Pascal's principle, which states that pressure applied to a confined fluid is transmitted undiminished in all directions.
 
• It uses brake fluid to transfer force from the brake pedal to the brake pads or shoes.
 
 
 
• **Brake Bleeding Process:**
 
 
• It involves removing trapped air from the hydraulic brake system to ensure proper brake function.
 
• Special tools and techniques are used to purge air bubbles from the brake lines and components.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Maintenance:**
 
 
• Regular inspection and maintenance of the brake system ensure safety and reliability.
 
• Using the recommended brake fluid type is essential for optimal performance.
